implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control (P06) was revised and approved 2026-09-22 and now covers OT explicitly. The OT access procedure (console accounts, remote sessions, SIS engineering access, driver cards) is due 2026-12-31 as part of the OT security standard (STD-01).

IT accounts (historian clients, remote access gateway users) come from the identity provider, which is fed by the HR system. DCS, SIS, terminal, and loading bay accounts are local and are created and removed by hand by the controls engineers. Engineering accounts are named (2024). Gaps: operators share one account per console position; OT accounts and loading bay driver cards are reviewed only once a year; P07 found 3 DCS accounts and 2 driver cards of people who had left (P07 AC-2).
evidence: DCS user export 2026-08-19; driver card list 2026-08-12; termination tickets
regulatory_driver: C-CHEMICAL-R02 (33 CFR 101.650(a)(5); 33 CFR 101.650(a)(7)); C-CHEMICAL-R01 (27.230(a)(8), voluntary benchmark)

implementation_statement: The identity provider disables IT accounts after 45 days without use. Local DCS, SIS, and terminal accounts have no inactivity check; a quarterly stale-account report from each OT system starts 2026-10.

The DCS enforces four roles (operator, shift supervisor, engineer, administrator) on every console and controller write. The SIS controllers accept logic downloads only with the keyswitch in program and only from the SIS engineering workstation on the SIS network. Recipe edits in the batch management system need the recipe author role.
evidence: DCS security configuration export; SIS keyswitch log; P07 AC-3 test

implementation_statement: The IT/OT firewall pair (2023) enforces zone rules between the business network, the OT DMZ, the supervisory zone, the control zone, and the SIS zone. Business-to-control traffic is denied; order data reach the batch system only through the relay in the OT DMZ. Gap: 7 of 214 rules were broader than documented, and the tank gauging server web interface was reachable from the whole supervisory zone (P07 SC-7).

Recipe release needs two approvals (author and a second chemist) in the batch management system. DCS and SIS logic changes need MOC approval by the Process Safety Manager and a different person to load the change. Firewall changes are requested by the OT Security Engineer and approved by the Controls Engineering Manager.
evidence: Recipe release workflow log (25 sampled releases); MOC records

implementation_statement: OT roles follow least privilege for named engineering and supervisor accounts. Gap: shared operator console accounts mean actions cannot be tied to one person, and 2 integrator accounts on the gateway had standing rights to all OT zones instead of the zones they support.
evidence: DCS role matrix; gateway policy export

implementation_statement: DCS security settings, firewall rules, and gateway policies can be changed only by named administrators (3 controls engineers, the OT Security Engineer). Gap: the tank gauging server and the dock transfer PLC had no role separation (P07).
evidence: Administrator lists for DCS, firewall, gateway

implementation_statement: Engineers use separate operator-level accounts for routine monitoring. Two of the 5 controls engineers used their engineering accounts for monitoring during the P07 sample week.

Directory and cloud administrator credentials are held in the privileged access vault with check-out and rotation. OT administrator accounts are separate from the same people's IT accounts (separate credentials, 101.650(a)(6)).
The DCS logs engineering and administrator actions locally (90 days). Gateway sessions are recorded. Gap: DCS security logs are not sent to the SIEM and are reviewed only after an event.
evidence: DCS audit trail sample; gateway session recordings

implementation_statement: Tailored. Remote access gateway, historian client, and identity provider logins lock after 10 failed attempts. Operator consoles are not locked out, so an operator can always act during an upset; the staffed, badge-controlled control room compensates (SP 800-82 Rev. 3 tailoring). The USCG lockout requirement (101.650(a)(1)) applies to IT systems, which are covered.
evidence: Identity provider policy; gateway policy; tailoring record

implementation_statement: Tailored. Engineering workstations and historian clients lock after 10 minutes. Operator consoles in the control room do not lock, by design, for safety; the room is staffed at all times.

All vendor and engineer remote access to the Port PCBMS goes through the OT remote access gateway in the OT DMZ (2024): named accounts, MFA, per-session approval by the Shift Supervisor, and recording. Each remote path has a documented justification (101.650(e)(3)(v)). Gap: approvals were by phone and were not logged for 6 of 20 sampled sessions.
regulatory_driver: C-CHEMICAL-R02 (33 CFR 101.650(a)(4); 33 CFR 101.650(e)(3)(v); 33 CFR 101.650(f)(3)); C-CHEMICAL-R01 (27.230(a)(8), voluntary benchmark)

implementation_statement: Every gateway session is recorded and the session log goes to the SIEM. Gap: recordings are reviewed only on request; monthly review of third-party sessions starts 2026-10 (101.650(f)(3)).
evidence: Gateway session log in the SIEM

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote sessions are encrypted end to end from the user to the gateway and from the gateway to the target.
The gateway is the only managed access control point for remote access into the Port OT zones; the firewall denies all other inbound remote protocols.
evidence: Firewall rule export; P07 SC-7 test

implementation_statement: Privileged remote commands (logic downloads, firmware updates) are allowed only during sessions approved under MOC. Gap: the approval check is procedural; the gateway does not block a download in an unapproved session.
No wireless access is allowed in the control or SIS zones. A wireless survey of the control room, Blend Hall 1, and the tank farm in 2026-07 found no rogue access points.
Vendor laptops may connect to OT only on site, after a scan at the media kiosk and under escort. Gap: no written terms of use for vendor laptops during turnarounds.
evidence: Visitor and contractor log; kiosk log

implementation_statement: All staff take annual awareness training; Port plant staff also take the USCG module (Cybersecurity Plan provisions, threat recognition, circumvention techniques, reporting to the CySO, OT topics). Gap: 371 of 430 Port employees and no tracked contractors had completed it by the 2026-01-12 deadline (101.650(d)(4)); 412 of 430 complete on 2026-08-31.

Key personnel (controls engineers, OT Security Engineer, shift supervisors, CySO and alternate) receive role training on cyber incident duties (101.650(d)(2)). Gap: shift supervisors on 2 of 4 shifts have not had it; contractor key personnel are not tracked.
Training records are kept in the training platform for employees. Contractor training is not recorded (101.640 requires training records).

Logged today: firewall, gateway, historian, and DCS server Windows events to the SIEM; DCS security audit trail locally. Not logged: controller-level changes outside the DCS audit trail, tank gauging server, dock transfer PLC, SIS engineering workstation.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews IT and cloud alerts 24x7. IT/OT conduit logs and OT sensor alerts reach the SIEM, but the MSSP contract excludes OT and nobody reviews conduit logs; sensor alerts are watched by the OT Security Engineer in business hours only (gap 4).
evidence: MSSP statement of work; SIEM review record (none for OT)

implementation_statement: DCS servers, controllers, SIS, and firewalls take time from two GPS-referenced time servers in the supervisory zone.
Logs in the SIEM are accessible only to the security team and the MSSP. Local DCS audit trails can be cleared by a DCS administrator (P07 AU-9).
evidence: SIEM role list; DCS administrator rights

implementation_statement: SIEM retains 12 months online. DCS local audit trails roll over after 90 days, which is shorter than the 2-year record period the FSP sets under 33 CFR 105.225.
evidence: SIEM retention setting; DCS log settings

implementation_statement: Audit generation is enabled on the DCS servers, historian, gateway, and firewalls. To add: tank gauging server, SIS engineering workstation, and the batch system recipe audit log export.

The co-sourced internal audit firm assessed 36 controls in 2026-08 with an OT specialist subcontractor, independent of the teams that run the controls (P07). The annual Cybersecurity Plan audit (101.630(f)) will use the same independent assessors.

Internal interconnection terms exist for the ERP order relay and the historian replica (2023 design record). Gap: no written terms for the cloud data platform feed or for vendor gateways; interconnection register due 2026-12-31.
PCBMS weaknesses are tracked in the P07 POA&M with owners and dates and reported to the audit committee each quarter. This also serves 101.630(c)(12), documentation of unresolved vulnerabilities.
Monthly metrics to the COO (patch age, open POA&M items, gateway sessions). Gap: no continuous monitoring of OT configuration; OT monitoring strategy due with STD-03.

An external penetration test of internet-facing IT is done each year (last 2026-03). Gap: no test of the OT DMZ or the gateway; a USCG-scoped penetration test is needed with Cybersecurity Plan renewal (101.650(e)(2)) and is planned for 2027-05 so the results feed the FSA.

Internal connections inside the OT zones are documented in the 2023 network map. Gap: the map does not show the 6 loading bay controllers or the tank gauging server's second interface (101.650(b)(4)).

Configuration baselines exist for DCS controllers, servers, and operator stations (vendor-hardened image, 2024). Gaps: no baselines for the terminal PLCs, tank gauging server, or loading bay controllers.
The last 4 weekly offline copies of DCS, batch, and SIS configurations are kept in the Port plant fire safe; nightly online exports are kept for 30 days.
evidence: Fire safe log; export job history

implementation_statement: MOC covers DCS and SIS logic, setpoint, and alarm changes (2024), so control changes get a safety review, authorization, and updated procedures. Gaps: firewall and gateway changes use the IT change process with no safety review; terminal PLC changes are not in MOC (2 of 15 sampled changes had no MOC).
evidence: MOC log (15 sampled); IT change records

implementation_statement: The MOC form requires a process safety impact review and, since 2025, a security impact question for control system changes.

DCS logic changes need an engineering account and an EWS in the control room. SIS downloads need the keyswitch and the SIS engineering workstation. Gap: the SIS logic is compared with the approved copy only at the annual proof test, not after each change or monthly (gap 5).
evidence: SIS proof test record 2025-11-04; P07 CM-5 test

implementation_statement: DCS stations use the vendor-hardened image. Gaps: no written OT configuration standard (gap 14); the tank gauging server kept the vendor default administrator password (found 2026-08-19, changed 2026-08-20).

Unused services are disabled on DCS stations. Gaps: unused switch ports in Blend Hall 1 and the tank farm are not disabled (101.650(i)(2)); the tank gauging server runs a web service that is not needed from the supervisory zone.

Application allowlisting runs on the 8 operator stations and 2 EWS (2024). Gaps: not on the SIS engineering workstation, historian clients, or terminal HMIs; there is no written approved hardware, firmware, and software list (101.650(b)(1)).

The passive OT sensor (2025) discovered 412 Port OT assets; the controls team reconciled 340 into the asset register. Gaps: the register does not yet designate critical IT and OT systems (101.650(b)(3)) and lacks firmware versions for 72 devices.
Operators and engineers cannot install software on DCS stations (allowlisting and no local admin). Software is installed only by the controls team under MOC.

The Port plant emergency response plan (RMP 68.95) covers releases and evacuation. An OT contingency plan covering DCS, batch, SIS, and terminal recovery in BIA order (P05) is drafted and due 2026-12-31.
evidence: Emergency response plan; OT contingency plan draft

implementation_statement: Contingency training for controls engineers and shift supervisors on the OT contingency plan is planned after the plan is approved (2027-01).

Only one operator station has ever been restored from backup (2025). No full DCS or batch system restore has been tested, so the 12-hour RTO for the Ammonia Unit and Blend Hall 1 is unproven (P05 finding 1). A full restore test on spare hardware is set for 2026-11-10.
Weekly offline copies are kept in the Port plant fire safe; a second copy goes monthly to the Inland plant safe, 90 miles away.

The Inland plant can make the 15 highest-volume Blend Hall 1 formulations (about 20% of volume). Recipes are kept current in both systems by technical services. No alternate processing exists for the Ammonia or Peroxide Units; third-party supply is the fallback.

Nightly online export of DCS, batch, and SIS configurations to the backup server in the OT DMZ; weekly offline copy to removable media in the fire safe (2024). Historian data replicate to the cloud data platform.
evidence: Backup job logs; fire safe log

implementation_statement: Backup media are checked for readability each week. Gap: contents are not test-restored, and the SIS backup is not compared with the running logic (P07 CP-9).

Recovery order follows the BIA (P05 section 8): units held safe by the SIS, then tank farm levels, then the Ammonia Unit on a verified DCS. Spare controller and server hardware is on site. Gap: no tested rebuild procedure from clean media for the DCS server pair (P01 R-006).

The SIS places the Ammonia and Peroxide Units in a safe state independent of the DCS. Operating procedures cover holding the units isolated with manual valves and portable detection when the DCS is unavailable.
evidence: SIS safety requirements specification; operating procedures

implementation_statement: Engineering, administrator, and gateway users are uniquely identified. Gap: operators share one account per console position at both plants (gap 2).

MFA through the identity provider protects all IT access and every gateway session into OT (remotely accessible OT, 101.650(a)(4)). Local console logins in the control room do not use MFA; physical access control compensates.
evidence: Identity provider policy; P07 IA-2(1) test

implementation_statement: MFA applies to non-privileged gateway and IT users as well.
OT account names follow a naming rule for named accounts. Shared console identifiers remain (gap 2).

DCS passwords follow the 14-character standard where supported. Gaps: the tank gauging server default administrator password (found 2026-08-19, changed 2026-08-20); shared console passwords are changed only twice a year; dock transfer PLC uses a 4-digit PIN.

IT passwords follow the identity provider policy (14 characters, breached-password check). OT systems apply the same rule where technically possible; 3 device types cannot, and compensating measures are not yet documented (101.650(a)(2)-(3)).
evidence: Identity provider policy; OT exceptions list draft

implementation_statement: IT incident response training is annual. OT-specific incident training for shift supervisors and controls engineers starts with the 2026-11-17 joint tabletop.

No joint cyber and process emergency exercise has been held (gap 9). The first is set for 2026-11-17 and also counts as the RMP tabletop (68.96(b)(2)) and the annual USCG cyber exercise (101.635(c)). Two cyber drills a year start in 2027 (101.635(b)).

IT incidents are handled under the 2024 IR plan with the MSSP and the cyber insurer's panel. The OT runbook (P08 runbook 1) was approved 2026-09-22 and puts the shift supervisor and process safety first. Gap: not yet exercised.

Incidents are tracked in the IT ticketing system. OT events found by the sensor are kept in email; moving them to the incident register starts 2026-10 (101.640 records of cybersecurity threats and incidents).

MTSA reporting to the NRC and the COTP (33 CFR 101.305) is in the FSP. Gap: cyber incident reporting under 33 CFR 6.16-1 (FBI, CISA, COTP, immediately) is not in the FSP procedures (gap 9). Fixed in P08; FSP amendment due 2026-12-31.
evidence: FSP reporting section; P08 notification matrix

implementation_statement: The MSSP provides 24x7 IT incident support; the cyber insurer's panel provides forensics and breach counsel. The DCS vendor's incident response service is on contract for OT forensics.
evidence: MSSP contract; insurance policy; DCS vendor service schedule

implementation_statement: The 2024 IR plan is IT-focused. Two runbooks (P08) were approved 2026-09-22; the Cyber Incident Response Plan for the Cybersecurity Plan will be built from them (101.620(b)(6)).
OT maintenance follows the mechanical integrity program; SIS proof tests are yearly (last 2025-11-04) and documented.
Vendor maintenance laptops are scanned at the media kiosk before use. Gap: vendor tools are not inventoried and some stay connected after turnarounds.
Remote maintenance by the DCS integrator, SIS vendor, and tank gauging vendor goes through the gateway with MFA and recording. Gap: monthly review of vendor sessions not yet done (101.650(f)(3)).
Vendor technicians on site hold a TWIC or are escorted under the FSP. Gap: escorts are not trained to recognize OT tampering.
Offline configuration media are kept in the fire safe with a sign-out log. Gap: SSI and legacy CVI are on file shares open to 65 users (gap 10).
evidence: Fire safe log; share permission report

implementation_statement: USB storage is blocked on DCS stations by policy and allowlisting. A media scanning kiosk is in the control room. Gap: USB ports are open on 14 local HMIs in Blend Hall 1 and packaging.
Unescorted access to the Port plant requires a TWIC and a company badge (FSP). Access to the control room, server room, and SIS cabinets is limited to an authorized list.
Badge readers protect the control room, the OT server room, and the rack rooms. Gap: 4 remote I/O cabinets in the tank farm and Blend Hall 1 use keyed locks with no access log (101.650(i)(1)).
Cameras cover the control room and server room entrances. Gap: the video management server sits on the business network (P01 R-035).

UPS on the DCS, SIS, and control room; one generator for the control room and emergency lighting. Gap: ammonia gas detectors in the tank farm run on UPS only (about 2 hours); EPA's standby power requirement for release detection monitoring applies by 2027-05-10 (40 CFR 68.67(c)(3); 68.10(g)(1)).
This SSP (approved 2026-09-22) documents the PCBMS. It will form most of Sections 6 to 9 of the Cybersecurity Plan.
All users accept POL-05 Acceptable Use each year; OT users also sign the control room rules (no personal devices on consoles).

The 2023 OT architecture follows SP 800-82 Rev. 3 zones and conduits. Gap: the SIS network shares the firewall pair with the control zone rather than a dedicated device; to be reviewed in the Cybersecurity Assessment.
The risk management strategy and appetite statements in P01 were approved by the CEO on 2026-09-22 and cover OT and process safety.
Background checks at hire; TWIC for unescorted Port access (FSP). Job applicants handling 50% peroxide shipments are screened under the DOT security plan (49 CFR 172.802(a)(1)).
Terminations disable identity provider accounts the same day. Gap: OT accounts and driver cards are removed by hand from a checklist (P07 found misses).
Transfers trigger an IT access review. OT roles are not reviewed on transfer.
Contractor security duties are in the DCS integrator and SIS vendor contracts. Gap: no vulnerability or incident notice clause (gap 7) and no training requirement for contractor personnel.
This SSP categorizes the PCBMS (section 6). Critical IT and OT systems must be designated by the CySO in the Cybersecurity Plan; draft list in section 9.

The enterprise risk assessment (P01, 2026-07) covers the PCBMS, using SP 800-30. The USCG Cybersecurity Assessment (101.650(e)(1)) has not started; due 2027-07-16. Cyber-initiated scenarios are not yet in the Ammonia Unit HAZOP (next revalidation 2028-05).

Quarterly authenticated scans of IT and the OT DMZ. The passive OT sensor flags known vulnerabilities in OT assets. Gaps: no tracking of OT assets against CISA's KEV catalog (101.650(e)(1)(iv), (e)(3)(i)); no method to receive publicly submitted vulnerabilities (101.650(e)(3)(ii)).
The BIA (P05) ranks Port processes and dependent systems. A list of critical IT and OT systems as the rule defines them (could result in a TSI) is drafted.
Cybersecurity questions are part of IT procurement. Gap: OT purchases (the 2027 DCS upgrade, loading bay controllers) do not yet use cybersecurity criteria (101.650(f)(1)).
SOC 2 reports are reviewed for 3 of 11 key SaaS vendors (P09). OT vendors (DCS integrator, SIS vendor, tank gauging vendor) have no security review.

9 OT workstations run an end-of-support operating system (5 at the Port plant: 4 packaging line HMIs and the dock HMI; 4 Inland SCADA HMIs). They are isolated behind allowlisting at the Port plant only. Replacement planned at the 2027 turnaround.

Firewall pair between business and OT; OT DMZ for the historian replica, gateway, order relay, and backup server. Gap: the radar tank gauging server's web interface was reachable from the whole supervisory zone and 7 rules were broader than documented (P07 SC-7).
regulatory_driver: C-CHEMICAL-R02 (33 CFR 101.650(h)(1); 33 CFR 101.650(e)(3)(iv); 33 CFR 101.650(e)(3)(v)); C-CHEMICAL-R01 (27.230(a)(8), voluntary benchmark)

implementation_statement: Three conduits cross the IT/OT boundary (order relay, historian replica, gateway); all others are denied.

control_name: Deny by Default — Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny by default between all OT zones. Gap: 7 rules broader than documented.

Gateway sessions, historian replication, and the order relay are encrypted. Controller-to-server protocols are not encrypted (not supported by the DCS release); physical and zone controls compensate (101.650(c)(2) when technically feasible).
The SIS and DCS are designed to fail to a safe state: loss of controller communication trips the units to safe positions.
USB and unused network ports are disabled on DCS stations by device control. Gap: 14 local HMIs and unused switch ports in the field remain open (101.650(i)(2)).

OT patches are applied at the annual turnaround after vendor qualification. Gaps: the DCS is one major release behind; KEV-listed flaws are not handled without delay (101.650(e)(3)(i)); 9 end-of-support workstations (gap 6).
regulatory_driver: C-CHEMICAL-R02 (33 CFR 101.625(d)(15); 33 CFR 101.650(e)(3)(i)); C-CHEMICAL-R01 (27.230(a)(8), voluntary benchmark)

implementation_statement: Vendor-qualified antivirus with weekly signature updates through the OT DMZ on DCS stations; allowlisting on operator stations and EWS. Gap: terminal HMIs and historian clients have neither.

Passive OT sensor at the Port plant (2025), IT/OT firewall logs to the SIEM, MSSP 24x7 for IT. Gaps: OT alerts go to email in business hours only, conduit logs are not reviewed (101.650(h)(2)), and the Inland plant has no OT monitoring (gap 4).
evidence: Sensor configuration; MSSP statement of work
regulatory_driver: C-CHEMICAL-R02 (33 CFR 101.650(h)(2); 33 CFR 101.650(f)(3)); C-CHEMICAL-R01 (27.230(a)(8), voluntary benchmark)

implementation_statement: The Security Analyst receives CISA ICS advisories and the DCS vendor's security notices. Gap: alerts are not matched to the OT asset register or the KEV catalog.
The DCS checks controller firmware signatures. Gap: SIS logic and batch master recipes are not routinely compared with approved copies (P01 R-008).
evidence: DCS firmware check; SIS proof test record

implementation_statement: Operating procedures define fail-safe actions for loss of DCS view, loss of SIS communication, and loss of tank levels (manual gauging, transfer stop).
An OT supply chain risk plan is planned with the vendor standard (STD-04), due 2027-03-31.
DCS updates are obtained from the vendor portal with hash checks since 2025. Integrator-built logic is reviewed under MOC.
Spare DCS hardware is bought only from the DCS vendor. Loading bay controllers are bought through a distributor without provenance checks.
Supplier reviews happen at onboarding only (gap 7). Annual reviews of the DCS integrator, SIS vendor, tank gauging vendor, and the MSSP start in 2027-Q1.
Contracts with OT vendors do not require notice of vulnerabilities or incidents (101.650(f)(2)). New clause drafted by the General Counsel; to be added at renewal or by amendment by 2027-03-31.
DCS spare parts and software come from the vendor portal with hash verification. Gap: no check for the tank gauging and loading bay firmware.
